Anthracnose.quote: Leaf lesions (spots) begin as water soaked and then become yellowish circular spots.
Stem lesions on cantaloupe can girdle the stem and cause vines to wilt.
Circular, black, sunken cankers appear on watermelon measuring 1/4 to 1/2 in. (6 to 13 mm) in diameter and up to 1/4 in. (6 mm) deep.

Bacterial_Fruit_Blotch.quote: Water-soaked areas on the underside of cotyledons can be seen, and lesions on the hypocotyl cause collapse of the emerging plant.
Small, dark brown, somewhat angular and water-soaked lesions can appear, but they are generally inconspicuous.
Characteristic symptoms on fruits appear as dark olive green stain, or blotch on the upper side of the fruit.

Downy_Mildew.quote: Cucurbit downy mildew is easily recognized by its characteristic mosaic pattern of chlorosis and necrosis (dead cells) on the upper surfaces of cucurbit leaves
gray spores called sporangia that result in a fuzzy or downy appearance on lesions located on the underside of leaves.

Gummy_Stem_Blight.quote: Leaf lesions are round or triangular, particularly those at leaf edges, brown on melons and dark brown on watermelon.
young cankers start as water-soaked, green lesions, then become dry, rough, and cracked.
The flesh becomes watery and discolored

Phytophthora_Blight.quote: Symptoms on cucumber, muskmelon, and watermelon are normally found on leaves and fruit.
Lesions on stems are constricted, darkened, and water-soaked, often extending a few inches above the soil line
Circular lesions are common on fruit and will appear water-soaked and sunken

Powdery_Mildew.quote: Symptoms occur on both leaf surfaces, stems, and petioles as white, powdery fungal growth.
